The Wedding
Jaipur. A lake palace. Nine hundred guests, four drone cameras and a twelve-tier cake that Nikhil calls "content".
Captain, I'm your vice-captain, your best man and the only person here who knows this is fake. I'd like a raise.
Also your Dadi just arrived from Amritsar. Uninvited. With pickle.
Puttar! You marry a film star and you tell me on Instagram? On INSTAGRAM?
Where is she? I want to see if she can make a roti.
"Dadi, she's a superstar. She doesn't make rotis."
Protect Tara.
"Ask her yourself. She's braver than me."
Let them meet.
The varmala. Forty thousand flashes. Tara smiles at the cameras like she was born doing it. Maybe she was.
Smile. Lean in. Don't step on my lehenga, it costs more than your bat sponsorship.
The photographer shouts. "A kiss! For the fans!"
Kiss her cheek.
Respectful. The fans groan.
Kiss her properly.
It's for the cameras. Mostly.
Bow dramatically instead.
Make her laugh.
For the cameras. Only for the cameras. She forgets to pull away for one second too long. So do you.
She can't make a roti. But she asked me to teach her. Good girl. I like her.
Midnight. The music stops. A man walks in through the garden gate, uninvited, in a white sherwani, carrying a single red rose.
Tara. You forgot to invite your ex-fiancé. I forgive you.
Vivaan Rai, the actor who broke Tara's heart on live TV, just crashed your fake wedding.
